Proposition
[Geometric Interpretation of II] ↗ cor:gauss-formula-along-curve 1. ch8:8.10

Let $p\in M$ and $v\in T_pM$.

  1. $\mathrm{II}(v,v)$ is the ambient acceleration at $p$ of the $g$-geodesic $\gamma _v$.

  2. If $v$ is a unit vector, then $|\mathrm{II}(v,v)|$ is the ambient curvature of $\gamma _v$ at $p$.

Proof

\sketch For any regular $\gamma :(-\varepsilon ,\varepsilon )\to M$ with $\gamma (0)=p$ and $\gamma '(0)=v$, (8.2) gives

\[ \widetilde D_t\gamma ' =D_t\gamma '+\mathrm{II}(\gamma ',\gamma '). \]

For $\gamma =\gamma _v$, the intrinsic derivative vanishes. If $v$ is unit, the ambient acceleration norm is the ambient curvature.

□
